Surah "Al-Tin" (The Fig)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ He swears by them because they are marvelous among fruit-bearing trees. It is narrated that "a tray of figs was presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He ate from it and said to his companions: 'Eat. If I were to say that a fruit had descended from Paradise, I would say it is this, for the fruit of Paradise has no seeds (ʿajam). So eat of it, for it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout.'" And he said: "The olive is an excellent siwak (tooth-stick) from the blessed tree; it sweetens the mouth and removes the ḥufra (a pit-like condition)." And he said: "It is my siwak and the siwak of the prophets before me." And from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "It is this fig of yours and this olive of yours." It was also said: they are two mountains in al-Sham, which produce them.

ﷺ-free passage, so no honorifics. Need to translate: Qur'anic quote ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾ "And by Mount Sinai" (meaning of "Tur Sinin" — "and Mount Sinin"). Technical terms: i'rab (grammatical inflection) gloss first time. Keep Arabic words under discussion in Arabic script.

Translation:

﴿And by Mount Sinin﴾. The word "al-Tur" (ṭūr), which means the mountain, is put in an idafa (genitive construction) to "Sinin" (Sīnīn), which is the place (al-buq'ah). It is like "Sinun" (سِينُونَ) and "Birun" (بِيرُونَ), in permitting inflection (i'rab, grammatical case-marking) with the waw and the ya', in keeping the ya' as it is, and in making the nun move with the vowels of inflection.

(p-660) ﴿And this land of security﴾, meaning Makkah,

﴿al-Amin﴾, from "amina al-rajulu, amanatan, fa-huwa amin" (the man became trustworthy, trustworthiness, so he is trustworthy). Its trustworthiness is that it protects whoever enters it, just as the trustworthy person protects what is entrusted to him. The meaning of swearing by these things is to make clear the nobility of these blessed places, and the good and blessing that have appeared in them through the dwelling of the Prophets and the awliya' (friends of God). The place where the fig and the olive grow is the place of emigration of Ibrahim (Abraham), and the birthplace and upbringing place of 'Isa (Jesus). Al-Tur is the place from which Musa (Moses) was called. Makkah is the place of the House, which is "a guidance for the worlds," the birthplace of our Prophet, and his place of mission, (peace and blessings of God be upon them all). Or the first two are an oath by the place where revelation descended to 'Isa, the third is an oath by Musa, and the fourth is an oath by Muhammad (ﷺ). And the answer to the oath:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 95, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, We created man﴾, and he is a genus (jins),

﴿in the best of stature﴾, in the best of proportion (ta'dil) of his form and his shape, and the balancing (taswiyah) of his limbs.

Then We returned him to the lowest of the low. That is: then the outcome of his affair was, when he did not give thanks for the blessing of that good, upright, well-proportioned creation, that We returned him to the lowest of those who are low in creation and make-up, meaning the most ugly of those who are ugly in form, namely the people of the Fire. Or [it means] the lowest of those who are low among the people of the degrees (of Hell). Or [it means]: then after that shaping and beautifying, We returned him to the lowest of those who are low in beauty of form and appearance, for We reversed him in his creation, so that his back became bent after being straight, his hair turned white after being black, his skin became wrinkled, his hearing and sight failed, and everything about him changed: his walk became a shuffle, his voice a faint murmur, his strength weakness, and his vigor senility.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 95, verse 6:

﴿Except those who have believed and done righteous deeds, for them is a reward never to be cut off.﴾ The fa' (fa', the particle of consequence) has entered here, unlike in surah "al-Inshiqaq," in order to combine the two dialects. The exception is connected (muttasil) according to the first reading and disconnected (munqati') according to the second. That is: "But those who were righteous among the aged and the infirm, for them is a reward that is not cut off, for their obedience and their patience in enduring the trial of old age and decrepitude, and in bearing hardships, and in performing worship."

(p-661)

The address in ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgement after this?﴾ is to mankind, in the manner of iltifat (the shift of grammatical person), meaning: what is the cause of your denying the recompense after this decisive clarification and this shining proof? And the meaning is that the creation of man from a drop of semen, his being formed as a sound human being, his progression through the stages of growth until he becomes complete and mature, and then his being brought back down until he reaches the most abject old age, is a proof, and you see no clearer proof of the power of the Creator than this. Whoever is able to create man, and to do all of this, is not incapable of restoring him. So what is the cause of your denying the recompense? Or the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning: who would attribute falsehood to you after this proof? In this case "ma" carries the meaning of "man" (who).

Is not Allah the most just of judges?

This is a warning to the disbelievers, and that He will judge them according to what they deserve. It is derived from "al-hukm," which means judgment (al-qada').
